formation.explanation: Caller append buffers during Prepare or forwards to promised leader. Prepare quorum selects highest accepted round/length history; leader syncs it, preserves maximum reported decision boundary, appends pending work when not stopped, and sends AcceptSync. Accept-phase follower validates ballot, phase and sequence, persists entries and acknowledges accepted length. Leader stores one accepted index per pid and decides on configured write quorum, propagating Decide or piggybacking AcceptDecide. Reads classify entries by local decided index; application polls and consumes them.

context.explanation: BLE heartbeat rounds assess connectivity/happiness and propose ballots; manual attempt increments a ballot directly. SequencePaxos requires higher ballot before leader preparation and resets leader support. Higher Prepare flushes follower batches, persists promise, resets sequence and emits Promise. Lower-ballot accepts are rejected with NotAccepted; unseen higher accepts initiate recovery. New or recovered instances with stored promise enter Recover; equal-ballot Prepare is allowed there. Reconnect/gaps request prepare; ticks resend preparation and StopSign work. Configuration transition uses decided StopSign then caller constructs a fresh instance.

connection.explanation: Authority acquisition reads prior accepted history before creating new support: Promise metadata and optional log synchronization carry old accepted rounds and decisions into prepare quorum selection. AcceptSync reestablishes participation under a new ballot/session; old-ballot replies are excluded, old sequences ignored and gaps resynchronize. Stored decisions constrain selected history through maximum reported decided index; suffix/snapshot reconstruction must preserve its meaning. Pending leader proposals are appended after sync unless StopSign seals the log; followers forward buffered ordinary proposals after sync. Persistence and Snapshot traits supply history, while caller transport/ticks drive asynchronous propagation.
